svg.text: Candidate 02 — the live bug: one book id, two servers
Spec 37 steps 2.1–2.2 · this is the step the review called its top recommendation — it fixes real data loss, then unlocks the client work.
BEFORE — the private cache keys by bare book id
server A — book #7
volume 1, position 100
server B — book #7
volume 1, position 900
Both wrote the same row: "progress#7" —
spec 30 made the device library a union of per-server
shelves, so cross-server silence turned into silent overwrite.
Resume position from one library could land on another's book.
fix →
AFTER — one key format, server-scoped
a.example#7 ≠ b.example#7
• Same function the replica uses (replicaBookKey /
replicaScopedKey) — one format, one place
• Favourites got the same treatment (X.1)
• Legacy bare-id rows are read as fallback but
never copied forward — a legacy row doesn't say
which server it's from; guessing would be the bug twice
Step 2.1 was only allowed to fail first — a test that could not be called the new way (tsc: Expected 2-3 arguments, got 4) was the right red.
Step 2.2 landed in cee4ba2; the typecheck gate (step 0.1) is what made the collision visible as a compile error, not just a wrong value.
